claim: Token locations are half-open byte offsets: each lexer action sets start to the prior scanner offset and end to start plus the matched byte length.
author: yevbar

claim: A # starts a comment; comment state ignores content through an unescaped newline, supports backslash-newline continuation, and exits at EOF.
author: yevbar

claim: Reserved words and multi-character operators are distinct tokens, including //, ?//, assignment compounds, comparisons, .., and $__loc__.
author: yevbar

claim: Single-character punctuation recognized by the lexer is . ? = ; , : | + - * / % $ < and >.
author: yevbar

claim: Opening delimiters push delimiter-specific lexer states, while a closing delimiter returns INVALID_CHARACTER unless it matches the current state.
author: yevbar

claim: Format tokens have the form @ followed by one or more ASCII letters, digits, or underscores, and the token value excludes @.
author: yevbar

claim: The numeric rule returns one LITERAL candidate for one or more digits with an optional dot and zero or more following digits, or for a dot followed by one or more digits; either form may have an exponent whose optional sign must be followed by at least one digit.
author: yevbar

claim: A double quote matched by the unqualified rule in the initial or inclusive non-comment states pushes the exclusive string state and returns QQSTRING_START; comment state is exclusive and consumes quotes as comment content. In string state, \( pushes interpolation state and returns QQSTRING_INTERP_START, while a double quote pops string state and returns QQSTRING_END.
author: yevbar

claim: Identifiers and bindings may have repeated namespace segments ending in ::; field shorthand is a dot followed by one unqualified identifier, and binding token values exclude $.
author: yevbar

claim: ASCII space, carriage return, newline, and tab are ignored outside strings and comments; any other unmatched byte returns INVALID_CHARACTER.
author: yevbar

claim: false, true, and null match the general IDENT rule; the lexer has no active dedicated token rules for these spellings.
author: yevbar

claim: The field-access fixture evaluates .e0 and .E1 as the complete field names e0 and E1, but evaluates .E-1 and .E+1 as field E followed by subtraction or addition.
author: yevbar

claim: Pipe is the lowest declared expression operator and is right-associative.
author: yevbar

claim: Comma binds more tightly than pipe and is left-associative.
author: yevbar

claim: The // alternative operator binds more tightly than comma and is right-associative.
author: yevbar

claim: =, |=, +=, -=, *=, /=, %=, and //= share one nonassociative precedence tier above //.
author: yevbar

claim: Boolean or is left-associative and binds more tightly than assignment; boolean and is left-associative and binds more tightly than or.
author: yevbar

claim: ==, !=, <, >, <=, and >= share one nonassociative tier above boolean and.
author: yevbar

claim: Binary + and - are left-associative and bind more tightly than comparisons.
author: yevbar

claim: Binary *, /, and % are left-associative and bind more tightly than binary + and -.
author: yevbar

claim: Optional and postfix term forms use precedence tiers above binary arithmetic, with NONOPT below ? . [ and FIELD so specialized optional productions win over the general Term ? production.
author: yevbar

claim: Arithmetic associativity is fixture-visible: multiplication/division bind above addition, and repeated multiplicative or additive operators group left.
author: yevbar

claim: The fixture false, 1 // 2 confirms comma has lower precedence than //, so it groups as false, (1 // 2).
author: yevbar

claim: Unary negation consumes a Term, placing its operand above binary-expression tiers; calls, grouping, literals, and postfix indexing are Term forms.
author: yevbar

claim: Function definition binding has an explicit FUNCDEF precedence below pipe, and Query binds a parsed FuncDef over the following Query.
author: yevbar

claim: Unresolved: what grouping contract should be chosen for try/catch mixed with every lower-precedence operator not covered by fixtures, given the dedicated try and catch precedence declarations and three separate Term productions?
author: yevbar

claim: Field, quoted-field, bracket-index, iteration, and slice suffixes each have explicit optional and non-optional productions; optional variants lower to INDEX_OPT or EACH_OPT, while general Term ? wraps the whole term in try/backtrack.
author: yevbar

claim: Both .a[] and .a.[] chaining forms are accepted, and suffix ? suppresses iteration errors whereas the non-optional forms surface them.
author: yevbar

claim: Query admits function-definition binding, Expr as Patterns | Query binding, label binding, right-recursive pipe, comma, or a single Expr.
author: yevbar

claim: Variable binding requires Expr as Patterns | Query; Patterns can be a binding, nonempty array pattern, or nonempty object pattern, with ?// destructuring alternatives.
author: yevbar

claim: Empty array and object destructuring patterns are compile failures; the fixtures require the parser's token-specific verbose diagnostics and locations.
author: yevbar

claim: A label has grammar label BINDING | Query, and break requires a BINDING; a missing break binding gets a dedicated parser diagnostic.
author: yevbar

claim: A syntactically valid break using an ordinary variable name does not bind to that variable and later fails compilation as an undefined internal label symbol at the full break-expression span.
author: yevbar

claim: reduce grammar is reduce Expr as Patterns ( Query ; Query ).
author: yevbar

claim: foreach grammar is foreach Expr as Patterns ( Query ; Query ) with an optional third semicolon-separated Query.
author: yevbar

claim: Destructuring patterns are accepted in foreach and reduce bindings, including nested array/object patterns.
author: yevbar

claim: try has forms try Expr catch Expr and try Expr; a missing catch body has a dedicated unterminated-try diagnostic.
author: yevbar

claim: if grammar supports zero or more elif branches, an optional else body, and mandatory end; absent else lowers to an identity/no-op body.
author: yevbar

claim: Function definitions are def IDENT : Query ; or def IDENT ( Params ) : Query ;, and parameter and call argument lists are nonempty and semicolon-separated.
author: yevbar

claim: Function parameters distinguish IDENT filter parameters from BINDING value parameters, but call arguments are uniformly parsed as Query and wrapped as lambdas.
author: yevbar

claim: Functions can be redefined by arity and are lexically scoped; fixtures also preserve def f($a;$b) value-parameter syntax.
author: yevbar

claim: A top-level program is optional module metadata, zero or more imports, then either a Query or function definitions only; a parsed library rejects a main expression.
author: yevbar

claim: The parser semantic union contains only jv literal and compiled block values, and grammar actions immediately lower literals and syntax into blocks rather than constructing a source-level AST.
author: yevbar

claim: String interpolation is parsed as a sequence of constant text and formatted Query results combined by addition; the parser does not retain a string-segment source node.
author: yevbar

claim: jq promises to retain an original numeric literal spelling until the value is mutated, even though arithmetic results use a double-precision representation.
author: yevbar

claim: Unresolved: which raw token spellings and delimiters must a new source-level AST retain for strings, numbers, object keys, and format strings, since the pinned parser immediately lowers them and only numeric spelling preservation is explicitly specified?
author: yevbar

claim: Grammar-symbol locations span from the first RHS symbol start to the last RHS symbol end; an empty production is positioned at the preceding symbol end.
author: yevbar

claim: Generated instructions initially have UNKNOWN_LOCATION, and gen_location fills only instructions that still lack a location while retaining the source locfile.
author: yevbar

claim: Source locations are attached selectively to break, variable loads, identifier calls, explicit calls, and some object entries rather than to every grammar reduction.
author: yevbar

claim: $__loc__ lowers to an object containing the source filename and one-based line number computed from the token start; it does not include a column or end position.
author: yevbar

claim: Located diagnostics report one-based line and byte-column, echo the source line, clamp the highlighted span to that line, and draw at least one caret.
author: yevbar

claim: An UNKNOWN_LOCATION diagnostic omits source name, line, column, source echo, and caret.
author: yevbar

claim: The parser requests verbose syntax errors, increments an error counter for each yyerror, and formats parser errors through locfile_locate with a jq: error: prefix.
author: yevbar

claim: Invalid LITERAL or string-text values produce their JSON-parser message at the token span, then are replaced with null for recovery; any accumulated parse error discards the complete compiled block.
author: yevbar

claim: Undefined variables, calls, and internal break labels are compile errors reported at instruction source spans, with distinct message templates.
author: yevbar

claim: Fixture-visible locations highlight the complete offending grammar span for semantic errors, including parenthesized object keys, undefined variables, and nonconstant metadata.
author: yevbar

claim: An unterminated delimited construct preserves jq's fallback diagnostic at its opening source delimiter rather than synthesizing a zero-width span at EOF; string parsing applies the same opening-delimiter contract only after all preceding string text and escape tokens were valid.
author: codex-language-string-literals-eof-fixer

claim: A line exactly %%FAIL marks the next program as required to fail compilation and requires its complete captured jq: error message to match subsequent nonblank fixture lines.
author: yevbar

claim: A line exactly %%FAIL IGNORE MSG marks the next program as required to fail compilation but disables message comparison.
author: yevbar

claim: The compile-failure callback retains only messages beginning jq: error, in a fixed 4096-byte buffer, so parser compatibility fixtures observe the last such reported message rather than an arbitrary diagnostic object.
author: yevbar

claim: For %%FAIL message checks, each expected nonblank line must prefix-match the remaining captured message in order, and any uncaptured suffix makes the fixture invalid.
author: yevbar

claim: Compile-failure fixtures preserve exact verbose token names, filename, one-based line and column, four-space source indentation, caret indentation, and caret count.
author: yevbar

claim: The numeric rule has no leading sign: + and - are returned by the earlier single-character rule. It admits leading zeros, a trailing dot after digits, and a leading dot only when a digit follows.
author: yevbar

claim: Dot and exponent edge spellings fall back to other rules when the complete numeric pattern cannot match: a bare dot is '.', two dots are REC, .e0 and .E1 are FIELD, and an exponent marker or sign without a following digit is not part of the preceding LITERAL.
author: yevbar

claim: Every numeric-rule match is passed to jv_parse_sized before the lexer returns it as LITERAL.
author: yevbar

claim: In string state, one or more non-interpolation escape candidates form one QQSTRING_TEXT token by being wrapped in double quotes and passed to jv_parse_sized.
author: yevbar

claim: Unescaped string bytes form QQSTRING_TEXT directly through jv_string_sized rather than JSON parsing; the string-state catch-all returns INVALID_CHARACTER only for a byte unmatched by the escape, raw-text, interpolation-start, and quote rules.
author: yevbar

claim: Interpolation and nested (, [, and { delimiters use the lexer state stack and must close in LIFO order, and only the ) that closes interpolation returns QQSTRING_INTERP_END. The generated default EOF action terminates scanning in the initial, delimiter, interpolation, and string states without returning a synthetic closing boundary.
author: yevbar

claim: The bare IDENT Term action lowers exactly false, true, and null to constants; other bare identifiers become calls, and the separate IDENT '(' Args ')' production is a call action rather than literal lowering.
author: yevbar

claim: The lexer rules make .E-1 and .E+1 begin with FIELD .E followed by the separate '-' or '+' token and LITERAL 1, whereas .e0 and .E1 each match one longer FIELD token.
author: yevbar

claim: After scanning, the common parser wrapper diagnoses an invalid LITERAL or QQSTRING_TEXT value at that token span, frees the invalid value, and substitutes null for parser recovery.
author: yevbar

claim: jv_string_sized preserves valid UTF-8 bytes but replaces each badly encoded code point with U+FFFD, which is the conversion used for unescaped QQSTRING_TEXT.
author: yevbar

claim: jq_yy_scan_bytes copies every byte through the caller-supplied length, appends two end-of-buffer markers after those bytes, and routes an earlier byte 0 through the generated DFA real-NUL transition rather than treating it as EOF.
author: yevbar

claim: The common parser scans locations->length bytes, and module loading constructs that length with jv_string_length_bytes; therefore embedded byte 0 in a module is lexer input rather than a source terminator.
author: yevbar

claim: The current top-level compile entry constructs its locfile length with strlen, so any embedded-byte-0 truncation in that path occurs at the driver boundary before the explicit-length lexer is invoked.
author: yevbar

claim: Identity is a standalone Term, while parenthesized syntax contains a complete Query and lowers to that query.
author: codex-language-parser

claim: Field shorthand is accepted both as a standalone Term and as a suffix on another Term; the lexer token value excludes the leading dot.
author: codex-language-parser

claim: General postfix optional is a recursive Term production, so it can bind to a completed term repeatedly; specialized field-optional productions bind the question mark with field access.
author: codex-language-parser

claim: Query pipe and comma productions are governed by a right-associative pipe tier and a tighter left-associative comma tier.
author: codex-language-parser

claim: The common parser wrapper supplies an explicit byte length to the lexer and destroys the complete partial compiled block whenever any parse error accumulated.
author: codex-language-parser

claim: Postfix-dot field and error productions shift the dot before validating the following string or error token, while question mark is a separate single-byte lexer token.
author: codex-language-parser-fixer

claim: Pipe is declared right-associative, comma is declared left-associative at the tighter precedence tier, and a parenthesized Term contains a complete Query.
author: codex-language-parser-depth-fixer

claim: The generated pure Bison parser starts with 200 state/value/location stack entries, grows those stacks together through the jq allocator, caps built-in growth at 10000 entries, and takes the memory-exhausted path when no further growth is permitted; literal and block destructors release discarded semantic values.
author: codex-language-parser-depth-fixer

claim: A numeric LITERAL has no leading sign; '-' is a separate lexer token and the recursive '-' Term production accepts repeated unary minus such as --1 as nested source terms rather than folding a sign into the numeric token. The generated scanner action returns the matched single-byte punctuation directly.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: The numeric lexer rule accepts digit-leading integers and fractions including a trailing dot, dot-leading fractions, and exponents with an optional sign followed by one or more digits.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: The bare IDENT Term action maps exactly false, true, and null to constants; other complete identifiers and the IDENT '(' Args ')' form remain calls.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: The upstream jq compatibility suite directly exercises true, false, null, positive 1, and negative -1 as simple filters.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: The shared 10000-entry generated-parser stack accepts 9995 nested unary minuses but rejects 9996, accepts 9994 nested groups but rejects 9995, and for mixed groups followed by unary minuses accepts a combined depth through 9995; unary minuses before a group reduce that combined boundary to 9994.
author: codex-language-parser-stack-budget

claim: After a deeply prefixed term, the first recursive postfix optional occupies one additional live parser-stack entry while repeated postfix optionals do not add another high-water increment: unary-minus and group-then-minus combined boundaries become 9994 with one or more suffixes.
author: codex-language-parser-stack-budget

claim: Unary '-' consumes a complete recursive Term, so its operand includes identity, standalone field, postfix field and optional forms, grouped Query forms such as pipe and comma, scalar literals, and nested negation; pipe is right-associative while comma is the tighter left-associative Query tier.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: A pipe or comma Query operator at the deepest point of otherwise plain nested groups adds one live generated-parser stack entry relative to a single Term leaf: 9993 surrounding groups compile and 9994 reach the 10000-entry exhaustion path; already reduced unary prefixes do not remain live at that operator.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals

claim: The right-recursive pipe grammar retains two generated-parser stack entries per open pipe: pinned jq 1.8.1 accepts 4997-operator identity, numeric, and postfix-field chains and rejects 4998. Stack peaks are event-local: after 9994 nested groups reduce, an outer postfix still succeeds, while 9995 groups exhaust the stack at the opener.
author: codex-language-scalar-literals-fixer

claim: The lexer emits false, true, and null as ordinary IDENT tokens and discards intervening whitespace; the grammar distinguishes a bare IDENT Term from IDENT '(' Args ')', so keyword spelling alone does not select literal lowering when an opening call delimiter follows.
author: codex-language-scalar-call-fixer

claim: A double quote enters exclusive string state; plain text and grouped escape candidates become QQSTRING_TEXT, interpolation has a distinct start token, and the closing quote ends the state.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: String is assembled from start, zero or more text/interpolation segments, and end, and is accepted as a Term alongside LITERAL and unary minus.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: Invalid LITERAL and QQSTRING_TEXT decoder values are diagnosed at the complete token location, replaced with null for recovery, and any accumulated parse error discards the partial compiled block.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: The JSON string decoder accepts the eight JSON single-character escapes, decodes four hex digits, requires a low surrogate after a high surrogate, combines valid pairs, emits UTF-8, and gives distinct invalid escape, Unicode, surrogate, and raw-control messages.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: jq's UTF-8 decoder identifies invalid leads, continuations, truncation, overlong encodings, surrogate encodings, and values above U+10FFFF; its encoder emits one through four bytes.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: Unescaped QQSTRING_TEXT calls jv_string_sized, which preserves valid UTF-8 but replaces each badly encoded point with U+FFFD rather than rejecting the source.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: The compatibility suite covers JSON escapes and BMP Unicode, invalid-escape wording and caret width, interpolation, and embedded NUL strings in containment operations.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: String-related compile failures preserve the invalid escape token span while general compile-failure fixtures preserve byte-oriented source and caret locations.
author: codex-language-string-literals

claim: Observable jq 1.8.1 filter parsing accepts raw U+0000 through U+001F string-source bytes as lexer text, replaces each malformed raw UTF-8 decoding unit with U+FFFD, and replaces isolated low-surrogate escapes with U+FFFD; invalid escape letters, malformed or truncated Unicode escapes, and invalid high-surrogate pairing remain compile errors.
author: codex-language-string-literals-resume

claim: Adjacent escape candidates are decoded as one QQSTRING_TEXT token; the JSON string decoder walks that token in source order and returns immediately with the diagnostic for the first rejected escape, after accepting any preceding single-character, Unicode, surrogate-pair, or isolated-low-surrogate escapes.
author: codex-language-string-literals-fix

claim: StringStart followed by the empty or iterative QQString grammar adds a live generated-parser state beyond an ordinary one-token Term: checksum-pinned jq 1.8.1 probes accept completed empty, plain, escaped, Unicode, and malformed-raw-UTF-8 strings inside 9993 groups and exhaust the shared 10000-entry stack inside 9994, while a first-lookahead invalid escape at 9994 retains its lexical diagnostic before that state is entered.
author: codex-language-string-literals-stack-fix

claim: Binary + and - are left-associative, while binary *, /, and % are left-associative at the next tighter precedence tier; each has a distinct Expr production.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic

claim: Comma and pipe are looser Query productions, parentheses contain a complete Query, and postfix optional plus recursive unary minus are Term productions that bind before binary arithmetic.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic

claim: The arithmetic punctuation characters +, -, *, /, and % are returned as distinct single-byte tokens, while a numeric literal has no leading sign and may contain an exponent sign only as part of a complete exponent.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic

claim: Accepted arithmetic fixtures distinguish tighter multiplication and division from addition and demonstrate left grouping for repeated division, mixed multiplication/division, repeated subtraction, and mixed subtraction/addition.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic

claim: The generated parser shares capped state/value/location stacks and reaches its memory-exhausted path when they cannot grow; binary Expr productions retain parser state while their right operand is parsed.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic

claim: A comma Query retains generated-parser state while its tighter right-hand Expr is parsed: checksum-pinned jq 1.8.1 accepts 9991 unary minuses in `1,2+---3`-shaped probes and exhausts at 9992; surrounding group, postfix, suspended-pipe-plus-comma, and two-comma-across-group probes have neighboring 9990/9991, 9990/9991, 9989/9990, and 9988/9989 boundaries respectively.
author: codex-language-binary-arithmetic-fixer

claim: The lexer returns distinct two-byte tokens for !=, ==, <=, and >= before the single-character punctuation rule returns < and >, preserving longest-match tokenization.
author: codex-language-comparison-syntax

claim: The six comparison tokens share one non-associative precedence tier below arithmetic and above boolean and; each has a distinct Expr-to-Expr production.
author: codex-language-comparison-syntax

claim: The numeric comparison fixture directly exercises >, <, >=, <=, ==, and !=, while shtest lists compact expressions for all six among constant-folding probes.
author: codex-language-comparison-syntax

claim: The generated parser shares capped state/value/location stacks; checksum-pinned jq 1.8.1 comparison probes accept/reject unary-minus depths 9995/9996 on the left, 9993/9994 on the right, 9992/9993 inside one group, and 9991/9992 with a tighter arithmetic operator also pending on the comparison right side.
author: codex-language-comparison-syntax
